I used to get really angry (ex wife was a bitch). I had 2 modes...nothing, then pissed. There was no spectrum to my emotions. It took a few years, but the first step I learned was to not to react outwardly to something. then once I could get away from the situation safely and consistent, I started asking myself if the situation warranted anger. Often it didn't.

These days its not really that tough. I still step away and swear a lot, but usually, if it doesn't really warrant anger it fades pretty quickly.

Depends on the environment. Anger is one of my more powerful emotions. When available, I prefer a safe outlet, such as a punching bag or something that can be destroyed without causing harm to others. Doesn't matter if it's tearing apart an old, chewed up dog house or a broken down car, if nothing of value is lost in the destruction and no one is harmed by the act, I call it good.

If there's no physical objects for me vent on, I go for physical labor. Digging, clearing brush, moving shit, whatever. It gets a job done, can be financially rewarding, and hurts no one.

If neither of these options are available, I either meditate, take long walks in the woods, or play stupidly violent video games.

All else fails, I drink or smoke weed or both until the anger and the source are no longer relevant and let it all go.

My whole thing is not inflicting harm on people or things that don't deserve it, so keeping my anger in check and keeping my violence to a minimum are important to me.

I had a pretty bad temper when I was in my late teens. Punched the rearview mirror off my window after a night of indecisive teenagers driving me all over the place. But i had one moment where I smacked my little brother out of frustration. So I really put a lot of effort into getting that under control.

I'm not sure how well I can describe my process but the three main things I did was a personality purge, a mentality segmenting, and a mental buffer.

With the personality purge I spent nearly a year going into passive observation mode and inner reflection. I watch how others interacted with each other (real life, tv shows, books, whatever). Finding the interactions, behaviors, or vibes I liked or didn't like. Then tried connecting it with myself. Is that what I'm like when I'm mad? Is that the vibe i give off when I'm in a good mood? Am I projection my feelings with the right expressions? So I tallied up all the things I didn't like about myself, gathered them all up and burned them out with a cigarette. Kind of a symbolic/pain association thing, probably not the healthiest of things but I was young. Then I slowly rebuilt and tried emulating the things I liked from the observations.

Which lead into the mindset segmenting. It was a way to kind of force me into a different mentality to help me see things from a different perspective so I'll react differently. So if I needed to work hard I'd get myself in this "I'm gonna kick this days ass" competitive mode, if I wanted to be in a grinning like an idiot mindset I'd think back to some specific adorable moments. A lot of my interactions with gal friends was a bit of a dainty mindset based off of the interactions I saw with gay guys and straight girls, i liked the level of comfort and playfulness. Generally I maintained a strolling through the park mentality, the observation mode probably had a lot to it. I always thought of Shawshank Redemption where the guy is noted as walking through the prison yard like strolling through the park. The only time the temper was triggered was in specific cases of someone mistreating someone else, probably a bit of a hero complex on that one. But it was hard to control or force my head one way or another when emotions are instantly triggered.

So I worked on a mental buffer. This was mostly developed naturally with silly things like pretending I'm not ticklish so they stop trying or think it's not fair. During the observation mode there became a bit of a game to poke at me because I didn't get upset. So it would slowly escalate to find my breaking point, during the observation phase it was mostly due to feeling empty inside but it carried over into a dishish challenge to never give them the win. The big helper was scaring games. I was un-scarable, between observational habits and that dickish attitude to win. There was a lot of games around trying to scare me. I would jump internally but the delay would allow my brain to process it before the body reacted. Not a great fight or flight responce I tend to watch death coming rather than getting out of it's way. So I eventually applied that to my emotional responses.

My mom being an emotional tornado helped out a bit. I got to see the difference between controlling my emotions or my emotions controlling me.

So now I just stroll through the park and process before I react, which I'm generally too lazy to react. Anger is just too exhausting and I'd rather find the humor in it for a chuckle anyway. I've only been boiling angry a few times in the past 10 years. Sadly most of my mentalities have kinda just died off with nothing to charge them up. The biggest jump with quality of life was simply removing everyone who didn't make my life better and understanding they have their persuit of happiness and I have mine. Their actions shouldn't dictate mine and don't give the victory of knowing they have that power over you.

There may be a touch of my vindictive period of life in there. Whenever someone tries using me as a punching bag I knew them well enough to cut them deep with surgical precision.
